rationale: First candidate, no race data yet, so this is a conservative baseline. Geometry: five sensors spread across the 25 mm tape (x = -0.02 to +0.02 m, 0.01 m apart), placed 0.04 m ahead of the axle so the line is read before the wheels reach it. Sensor size 0.008 m keeps the footprint well inside the tape width. Chassis: 0.12 m wheel track, 0.03 m wheel radius, 0.12 m body width (widens the off-track limit to max(0.06, 0.0125 + 0.03) = 0.06 m), 0.16 m body length, 0.8 kg mass. Controller: sensor weights [-2, -1, 0, 1, 2] equal the sensor's lateral offset in cm, so the signal is roughly the line offset in cm and stays within +/-2. Positive weights go with left-side sensors, so a line on the left gives a positive signal and a left steer, as the contract requires. base_speed 1.6 targets the ~1.5 m/s average needed to finish in 3 s while staying below full PWM for some headroom in the bends. kp 3 gives a 1 cm offset about 1050 PWM of differential, a firm correction. ki 0.02 is small to avoid integral windup on the bends. kd 0.15 damps the oscillation expected from a high kp. line_loss 'last_direction' keeps the robot turning toward the side it last saw the line. Expected result: completion on the oval and s-bend, with some weaving on the slalom. I expect the main risks to be oscillation at kp 3 and running out of time if the speed is too low. Next measurements to check these: steering_oscillation and max_error (to judge kp/kd), completion_time and progress (to judge base_speed), and line_loss_events (to judge sensor coverage on the tighter bends).
